name: Question 19
worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=132$ and $n=441$, and we're given that

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(132,144)=3.
$$

Since $b=12$ is divisible by $3,$ our congruence has $3$ solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}132x & ≡12 &  & (\text{mod}\,441) \\ 3\cdot 44x & ≡3\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,3\cdot 147) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot 44x & ≡\cancel{3}\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 147) \\ 44x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,147)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in this new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=4$ and ${n}_{1}=147$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(4,147)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $147.$

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $44\,(\text{mod}\,147).$ To find the inverse of $44\,(\text{mod}\,147),$ we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}147 & = & 3\cdot 44 & + & 15\, & ⇔ & \,15 & = & 147-3\cdot 44 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 44 & = & 15\cdot 2 & + & 14\, & ⇔ & \,14 & = & 44-15\cdot 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 15 & = & 14\cdot 1 & + & 1\, & ⇔ & \,1 & = & 15-14\cdot 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 14 & = & 14\cdot 1 & + & 0\, &  & \, &  & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

$$
1=3\cdot 147-10\cdot 44
$$

We can write this result in modulo $147,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot 147-10\cdot 44 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ -10\cdot 44 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ (147-10)\cdot 44 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ 137\cdot 44 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,147)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse of $44$ modulo $147$ is $137.$

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $137,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}44x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ 137\cdot 44x & ≡137\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ x & ≡548 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ x & ≡3\cdot 147+107 &  & (\text{mod}\,147) \\ x & ≡107 &  & (\text{mod}\,147)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡107\,(\text{mod}\,147).$

But our original congruence was modulo $441$ (not modulo $147$). To find all the solutions modulo $441,$ we repeatedly add $147$ to $107$ modulo $441$ until we reach the number $107$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡107 &  & (\text{mod}\,441) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡107+147≡254 &  & (\text{mod}\,441) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡254+147≡401 &  & (\text{mod}\,441) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡401+147≡548≡441+107≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,441)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2,3}≡107,\,254,\,401\,(\text{mod}\,441).
$$

EXPLANATION

In the given congruence, we have a=132 and n=441, and we're given that gcd(a,n)=gcd(132,144)=3. Since b=12 is divisible by 3, our congruence has 3 solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

132x≡12(mod441)3⋅44x≡3⋅4(mod3⋅147)3⋅44x≡3⋅4(mod3⋅147)44x≡4(mod147)

Notice that in this new congruence, we have a1=4 and n1=147, where gcd(a1,n1)=gcd(4,147)=1. So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo 147.

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of 44(mod147). To find the inverse of 44(mod147), we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

147=3⋅44+15⇔15=147−3⋅44↙↙44=15⋅2+14⇔14=44−15⋅2↙↙15=14⋅1+1⇔1=15−14⋅1↙↙14=14⋅1+0⇔0=14−14⋅1

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

1=3⋅147−10⋅44

We can write this result in modulo 147, as follows:

3⋅147−10⋅44≡1(mod147)−10⋅44≡1(mod147)(147−10)⋅44≡1(mod147)137⋅44≡1(mod147)

Therefore, the inverse of 44 modulo 147 is 137.

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by 137, we get the following:

44x≡4(mod147)137⋅44x≡137⋅4(mod147)x≡548(mod147)x≡3⋅147+107(mod147)x≡107(mod147)

So, we get the solution x≡107(mod147).

But our original congruence was modulo 441 (not modulo 147). To find all the solutions modulo 441, we repeatedly add 147 to 107 modulo 441 until we reach the number 107 again:

x1≡107(mod441)x2≡107+147≡254(mod441)x3≡254+147≡401(mod441)x4≡401+147≡548≡441+107≡x1(mod441)

Therefore, the solutions are x1,2,3≡107,254,401(mod441).
